ordered_behavior: Capture raw index once, compute descriptor address once and retain it in ESI across children.
Compare current DWORD[ESI] with0. Nonzero branches to acquisition without initialization.
For zero, PUSH captured index and CALL00C11B5E. TEST returned EAX immediately, POP ECX to remove argument without changing those flags, then JNZ acquisition.

If initializer returned0, PUSH0x11 and CALL existing-name __amsg_exit at00BFBA09. The inspected parent contains POP ECX and acquisition continuation if it returns normally; no child no-return claim is made.

At the join, PUSH CURRENT DWORD[ESI] and CALL DWORD[00CE2218], labelled EnterCriticalSection. This is a second descriptor load even on the initial-nonzero route and must not reuse the compared pointer.
POP ESI; POP EBP; RET. No new status value or failure-result conversion.
path_consequences: Initial descriptor nonzero skips both direct children but still reloads the descriptor for the API.
Initializer nonzero suppresses failure child even if current descriptor is still0; parent performs no second non-null validation.
Initializer zero invokes failure child even if it published a nonzero descriptor; parent tests the returned EAX, not reread pointer, for this decision.
If the failure child returns, acquisition uses current descriptor unconditionally, even if0. Its actual return/termination behavior remains unresolved.

Mutating the original index argument after entry cannot select a different descriptor: ESI already captured the address. Mutating the descriptor through child/API/shared state can affect the later read.

No own writes to either descriptor DWORD, no direct replacement lock or allocator use, and no retry/spin loop. No extra callback dispatch is visible beyond the two direct children and one IAT call. Any initializer/failure callbacks, lazy publication race policy and child partial side effects remain unopened.
